name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor> convention: fd2_ prefix (game function) + wrap_ (accurately denotes a forwarding thunk) + the wrapped helper's descriptor (cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash). No Ghidra address residue (no hex suffix matching its own or any data address). Name correctly reflects the only behavior: transparently forward 3 args to fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash @ 0x35822.
purpose: Transparent forwarding thunk: passes its 3 stack args straight through to fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash @ 0x35822 and cleans them off the stack on return.
logic_summary: Binary body is exactly: CALL fd2_cinematic_chapter_portrait_dump_with_white_flash; ADD ESP,0xC; RET. No __CHK, no own stack frame, no semantics of its own. It exists purely as a layer-insertion / size optimisation: the ch27 turn-FF handler fd2_chapter_event_handler_3f__ch27_portrait_cutscene @ 0x358C7 pushes (0xF, 0x1B, 2) and tail-JMPs into this thunk at 0x358E5 to borrow its 0xC-byte cleanup tail instead of emitting its own. Ghidra's decompile shows arg reordering (in_stack_00000000 / arg1 / arg2) which is decompiler noise for a stack-arg JMP-target thunk; the machine code forwards all 3 stack args unchanged. The functionally-exact source is a plain cdecl forwarding wrapper, which Watcom lowers to the same push-args/call/cleanup/ret shape.
